title: A finite family of integral tensor elements descends along a directed colimit
statement: Let $I$ be a directed preorder, $(A_i)$ a directed system of commutative rings with colimit $A$ [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], and $i_0\in I$. Let $B_0,C_0$ be commutative $A_{i_0}$-algebras and $\varphi_0:B_0\to C_0$ an $A_{i_0}$-algebra map. Let $s\subset C_0$ be finite. If for every $x\in s$ the element $1\otimes x$ of $A\otimes_{A_{i_0}}C_0$ is integral over $A\otimes_{A_{i_0}}B_0$ through $\operatorname{id}_A\otimes\varphi_0$, then there exists $i\ge i_0$ such that every $1\otimes x$ with $x\in s$ is integral over $A_i\otimes_{A_{i_0}}B_0$ through $\operatorname{id}_{A_i}\otimes\varphi_0$. All algebra structures are induced by the transition maps and the colimit coprojection. No finite-type or module-finiteness assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tag 07RG, proof of Lemma 10.168.3, lifting monic polynomial coefficients and killing evaluations; checked at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07RG

proof.text: Restrict indices to the nonempty directed upper tail J = {i | i₀ ≤ i}. Equip each stage with its A₀-algebra structure. Tensor the transition maps and coprojections with the identity on B₀ and C₀. Functoriality and cocone naturality give compatibility; checking pure tensors proves commutation with φ₀ and preservation of 1 tensor x.

For one x choose a monic polynomial p over A tensor B₀ annihilating 1 tensor x. Represent the finitely many coefficients of p below its natural degree at stages using part (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-directed-colimit-base-change-elementwise] for B₀. Mathlib Finset.exists_le supplies a common upper bound in J, and transition maps transport all coefficients there.

Form q = X^p.natDegree plus the sum, indexed by Fin p.natDegree, of the lifted coefficient times X^k. Mathlib Polynomial.degree_sum_fin_lt and monic_X_pow_add show that q is monic, including degree zero and zero rings. Polynomial.Monic.as_sum and map compatibility show that q maps to p. Commutation of polynomial evaluation with ring homomorphisms makes the evaluation of q map to zero.

Apply part (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-directed-colimit-base-change-elementwise] for C₀ to this evaluation, giving a later stage where it is zero. Map q coefficientwise to that stage: Polynomial.Monic.map preserves monicity, and Polynomial.hom_eval₂ together with the commuting square shows that its evaluation is zero. This witnesses integrality of 1 tensor x at that stage.

Apply the previous argument to each x in the finite set s. Choose a common upper bound of the resulting indices in J with Finset.exists_le. RingHom.IsIntegralElem.map transports each witness there, and IsIntegralElem.of_comp discards the extra coefficient transition map. The transition maps fix 1 tensor x, giving simultaneous integrality. For empty s the upper tail is nonempty, so the same upper-bound argument applies.

lean.statement: theorem exists_integral_tensor_generators_of_colimit {I : Type u} [Preorder I] [IsDirected I (· ≤ ·)] (F : I ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}) [HasColimit F] (i₀ : I) (B₀ : Type v) (C₀ : Type t) [CommRing B₀] [CommRing C₀] [Algebra (F.obj i₀) B₀] [Algebra (F.obj i₀) C₀] (φ₀ : B₀ →ₐ[F.obj i₀] C₀) (s : Finset C₀) : letI : Algebra (F.obj i₀) (colimit F : CommRingCat.{u}) := (CommRingCat.Hom.hom (colimit.ι F i₀)).toAlgebra (∀ x ∈ s, (Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id (F.obj i₀) (colimit F : CommRingCat.{u})) φ₀).toRingHom.IsIntegralElem ((1 : (colimit F : CommRingCat.{u})) ⊗ₜ[F.obj i₀] x)) → ∃ (i : I) (h : i₀ ≤ i), letI : Algebra (F.obj i₀) (F.obj i) := (CommRingCat.Hom.hom (F.map (homOfLE h))).toAlgebra ∀ x ∈ s, (Algebra.TensorProduct.map (AlgHom.id (F.obj i₀) (F.obj i)) φ₀).toRingHom.IsIntegralElem ((1 : F.obj i) ⊗ₜ[F.obj i₀] x)
